calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Rangers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years, though.

calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Aho
calls.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Miller’s line (Cuylle, Miller and Kartye) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Robinson has a goal and an assist as the Hurricanes beat the Rangers
paras: Eric Robinson opened the scoring for the Hurricanes shorthanded midway through the first. Mika Zibanejad tied it up for the Rangers on the power play a little over a minute later. Jackson Blake and Alexander Nikishin scored four and a half minutes apart in the second half of the second to put the Canes up 3-1. Sean Walker pushed the lead to 4-1, 41 seconds later, in his 500th NHL game. With the goalie pulled and less than five minutes left, J.T. Miller cut Carolina’s lead to 4-2 on the power play. Jordan Martinook added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 5-2.

The Rangers were outshot 41-27, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. The Rangers hit two posts and the crossbar and still lost. Brandon Bussi made 25 saves for the Hurricanes, and Dylan Garand stopped 36 of 40 at the other end. The Hurricanes improved to 18-3-3, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Rangers fell to 13-9-1, slipping to fourth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Rangers’ three-game winning streak is over.
The Hurricanes have points in seven straight games (6-0-1).
The Rangers’ Sean Durzi was back in the lineup after missing eight games.
Max Sasson made his Rangers debut, after three seasons with the Canucks.
